lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 5 you met the Roman Empire. In which year did the Western Roman Empire end? (AD 476.) Today: what happened in the east, where the empire went on for almost 1,000 more years.

The Roman Empire was too big to rule from one place. In AD 330 Emperor Constantine made the old Greek town of Byzantium his new capital, Constantinople. After AD 395 the empire split for good into a western and an eastern half.
The west, weakened by many attacks, ended in 476. The east, which historians call the Byzantine Empire, lasted until 1453, when the Ottoman Turks took Constantinople: 1453 − 476 = 977 more years.

Constantinople stood where Europe meets Asia, on a narrow strait called the Bosporus. Traders came from both sides, so it grew rich. Huge land walls, built in the 400s, kept it safe for about 800 years. Today the city is Istanbul, in Turkey.

Its people spoke Greek but still called themselves Romans. The greatest emperor, Justinian, ruled from 527 to 565. His lawyers gathered hundreds of years of Roman laws into one clear set, finished in 534. Many countries' laws still grew from it.

Justinian also built the church of Hagia Sophia, finished in 537. Its dome was the biggest in the world for about 900 years. Byzantine artists covered walls with mosaics: pictures made of tiny pieces of coloured glass and gold.

Historians count in centuries: the years 401 to 500 are the 5th century, and the 1200s are the 13th century. A century is one more than the hundreds: AD 476 is in the 5th century, and 1453 in the 15th.

Try it in the world: build a city on both sides of a strait, with towers along its land wall. Put a great dome in the middle, and label each building with its century. Next: the Anglo-Saxons and the Vikings.

exercises.prompt: In AD 330, which town did Constantine make his new capital?
exercises.explain: He made Byzantium his capital and called it Constantinople, Constantine's city.

exercises.prompt: The Eastern Roman Empire ended in AD 476, at the same time as the west.
exercises.hint: Which half went on for almost 1,000 more years?
exercises.explain: False: the west ended in 476, but the east, the Byzantine Empire, lasted until 1453.

exercises.prompt: What language did most Byzantines speak?
exercises.hint: The eastern Mediterranean had spoken it since ancient Greece.
exercises.explain: Greek, even though they called themselves Romans.

exercises.prompt: Which emperor gathered the Roman laws into one clear set?
exercises.explain: Justinian: his code was finished in 534.

exercises.hint: It is a great city in Turkey.
exercises.explain: Istanbul, in Turkey, still on both sides of the Bosporus.

exercises.prompt: The Western Roman Empire ended in 476 and the Byzantine Empire in 1453. How many more years did the east last?
exercises.hint: Take the earlier year from the later one.
Look at where it stood, on the Bosporus.
choices: traders came from Europe and Asia
it was far from the sea
exercises.explain: It stood where Europe meets Asia on a busy strait, so traders passed through and paid taxes.

exercises.prompt: Put these in order, earliest first.
exercises.hint: Look at the years: the smaller the year, the earlier.
A century is one more than the hundreds in the year.
exercises.explain: 537 is in the 500s: 5 + 1 = 6, so the 6th century.

exercises.prompt: Match each name to what it is.
matches: a church with a huge dome
a picture of tiny glass pieces
exercises.hint: Which is water, which a building, which art and which law?
exercises.explain: Hagia Sophia: a church with a huge dome. A mosaic: a picture of tiny glass pieces. The Bosporus: a strait. Justinian's Code: a set of laws.

exercises.prompt: Hagia Sophia was finished in 537. A bigger dome was finished in Florence, Italy, in 1436. For how many years was Hagia Sophia's dome the biggest?
exercises.hint: Take the earlier year from the later one.

exercises.prompt: Which of these years is in the 15th century?
exercises.hint: The 15th century is the years 1401 to 1500: the 1400s.
exercises.explain: 1453 is in the 1400s, the 15th century. 1540 is in the 16th, 1399 in the 14th, 1066 in the 11th.

exercises.hint: Who did they believe they still were?
exercises.explain: False: they called themselves Romans. Historians named them Byzantines much later, after Byzantium.

exercises.prompt: Constantinople had water on three sides. Why were its land walls so important?
exercises.hint: Where could an army walk up to the city?
choices: they guarded the only side open to land
exercises.explain: Water guarded most of the city, so the great land walls on the one open side kept it safe for about 800 years.

exercises.prompt: Sort these: from the Byzantine Empire, or from Rome before it?
exercises.hint: The Byzantine Empire is the eastern empire after AD 395, ruled from Constantinople.
exercises.explain: Byzantine: Hagia Sophia, Justinian's Code, the land walls. Rome before: Hadrian's Wall (AD 122) and the Colosseum (AD 80).
